title: Understanding student and temporary worker numbers in Canada (data as of 31 March 2026)
key_claim: New international student arrivals to Canada fell 79% in January-March 2026 versus the same period in 2024 (down 42,465); meanwhile former temporary residents accounted for 59% of all new permanent residents in Q1 2026 (up from 44% in 2024 and 48% in 2025), most admitted through economic programs such as Express Entry and the Provincial Nominee Program.
verbatim_quote: 79% fewer new student arrivals between January and March 2026, compared to the same period in 2024
notes: Tier 1 government data. Anchors both the collapse in the student inflow and the funnel itself (former temporary residents now the majority of new PRs).

title: Long-term international migration, provisional: year ending December 2025
key_claim: UK long-term net migration for the year ending December 2025 was 171,000, nearly halving from 331,000 a year earlier; total long-term immigration fell 20% to 813,000, with non-EU+ work arrivals down 47%; 159,000 former study-visa holders emigrated, 57% of all non-EU+ long-term emigration.
notes: Tier 1 official statistics. Shows the UK arrivals collapse and the emigration of the 2022-23 student cohort that drives unusually low net migration.

title: NFAP Policy Brief: U.S. Labor Force Analysis (January 2025 to February 2026)
date_evidence: National Foundation for American Policy March 6, 2026
key_claim: The U.S. foreign-born labour force fell by about 1,008,000 from its March 2025 peak (596,000 since January 2026 alone); NFAP estimates restrictive immigration policy could remove roughly 19 million worker-years from the U.S. economy by 2028, underscoring that immigrants and international students supply most U.S. labour-force growth.
notes: Tier 2 think-tank analysis used as the single structural anchor (3-6 month band). Provides the labour-supply framing: immigration restriction is already shrinking the U.S. workforce.

title: Beyond volume: what HEPI's report on demographic decline means for international student recruitment strategy
key_claim: Drawing on HEPI report 201, the analysis warns England's 18-year-old population will fall around 18.5% by 2042 after a peak near 2030, potentially costing non-higher-tariff universities up to 29% of home undergraduate income and deepening their dependence on international postgraduate recruitment; it cautions that international demand growth can 'no longer be assumed'.
notes: Tier 2 policy-institute analysis. Supports the demand/finance dimension and supplies counter-argument material on institutional dependence and demand assumptions.

title: UK study visa issuance falls 32%
key_claim: UK Home Office data show study visa applications down 30% and sponsored study visa issuance down 32% in Q1 2026 year-on-year, with refusal rates sustained (over 40% for Pakistani applicants); new Basic Compliance Assessment 'RAG' thresholds take effect 1 June 2026, and April marked the seventh consecutive month of year-on-year study-visa falls.
notes: Tier 3 specialist trade press reporting UK Home Office statistics.

title: Student Visa Refusals Reached High of 35% Last Year
key_claim: U.S. F-1 student visa refusals reached a decade-high 35% worldwide in 2025 (India's rose from 36% in 2023 to 61% in 2025); new student visas issued from summer 2024 to summer 2025 fell 35.6%, which the report warns means 'a shrinking pipeline of globally trained talent entering the U.S. workforce'.
verbatim_quote: a shrinking pipeline of globally trained talent entering the U.S. workforce
notes: Tier 3 quality higher-education journalism reporting Shorelight and U.S. Department of State data.

title: The state of international enrollment in 6 charts
key_claim: U.S. new international enrolment fell 17% in fall 2025 (after -7.2% in 2024-25); international graduate enrolment fell 4.3% in spring 2026 (public four-year institutions -9.2%); Common App international applications for 2026-27 were down 9% as of 1 March; 84% of surveyed colleges cite restrictive visa policy as a significant challenge, and the State Department revoked roughly 8,000 student visas.
notes: Tier 3 journalism aggregating Open Doors/IIE, National Student Clearinghouse, Common App and NAFSA data; also documents institutional hedging (UC accepting 17% more international students).
